answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-reusable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one actor into a hundred identities multiplies the capital tied up; it does not multiply credible work. The glacier of locked funds moves slowly back into circulation, while a quill-signed audit trail links each penalty to evidence. At nadir, an attacker still loses real capital and time for every exposed identity.
